note: One plain-language definition per measurable / derived / event concept, written once and used by the 'what is X' answer.  A definition says what the quantity IS and what it is used for; the live value is read from the vehicle separately (resolve.py _define).  Nothing here is a number about this vehicle.

docs.motor_torque: The turning force the electric motor puts on the drivetrain, in newton-metres (Nm). It rises when you press the accelerator and goes negative when the motor recovers energy.
docs.motor_rpm: How fast the motor shaft spins, in revolutions per minute (rpm). It is proportional to road speed through the gear ratio.
docs.motor_power: The mechanical power at the motor shaft, in kilowatts (kW): torque times speed. It is lower than the battery power by the conversion losses.
docs.motor_temperature: The temperature of the drive motor windings or housing, in degrees Celsius. A high value means the motor is working hard or its cooling is limited.
docs.drive_mode: The driving state the car is in: parked, city driving, highway driving or charging.
docs.battery_power: The electrical power flowing out of (positive) or into (negative) the traction battery, in kilowatts (kW). Negative means charging or energy recovery while braking.
docs.battery_voltage: The voltage of the high-voltage traction battery pack, in volts (V). It falls slightly under load and rises as the pack charges.
docs.battery_current: The current flowing through the traction battery, in amperes (A). Positive is discharging, negative is charging or regeneration.
docs.battery_soc: State of charge: how full the traction battery is, as a percentage of its usable capacity.
docs.battery_temperature: The temperature of the traction battery pack, in degrees Celsius. The pack ages faster and charges slower when too cold or too hot, and a warning is raised when it is too hot.
docs.cell_temperature_max: The temperature of the hottest single cell in the battery pack, in degrees Celsius.
docs.cell_temperature_min: The temperature of the coolest single cell in the battery pack, in degrees Celsius.
docs.cell_voltage_min: The voltage of the weakest cell in the battery pack, in volts. A low value points at an ageing or unbalanced cell.
docs.battery_soh: The battery's present usable capacity as a percentage of its capacity when new (state of health). It falls slowly with age and use.
docs.charging_power: The power being delivered to the battery by the charger, in kilowatts (kW).
docs.regen_power: The power recovered by regenerative braking and sent back into the battery, in kilowatts (kW).
docs.coolant_flow: How much coolant the pump moves through the battery cooling circuit, in litres per minute. A drop means the pump or the circuit is degraded and the pack can overheat.
docs.hvac_power: The electrical power used by the heating and air-conditioning system, in watts (W).
docs.aux_battery_voltage: The voltage of the 12 V auxiliary battery that runs the lights, computers and door locks, in volts. Below about 12 V at rest it is weak.
docs.speed: How fast the car is moving, in kilometres per hour (km/h), from the wheel-speed sensors.
docs.steering_angle: How far the steering wheel is turned from straight ahead, in degrees. Negative and positive are left and right.
docs.steering_rate: How fast the steering wheel is being turned, in degrees per second.
docs.yaw_rate: How fast the car is rotating about its vertical axis, in degrees per second: how sharply it is turning.
docs.longitudinal_acceleration: Forward and backward acceleration of the car, in metres per second squared. Negative is braking.
docs.lateral_acceleration: Sideways acceleration of the car in a corner, in metres per second squared.
docs.brake_pressure: The hydraulic pressure in the brake system, in bar. It rises with how hard the brake pedal is pressed.
docs.brake_pedal: How far the brake pedal is pressed, as a percentage.
docs.accelerator_position: How far the accelerator pedal is pressed, as a percentage.
docs.tyre_pressure: The air pressure inside each tyre, in kilopascals (kPa), measured by the tyre-pressure monitoring system. It should match the pressure printed for this car, because low pressure raises energy use and tyre wear.
docs.tyre_temperature: The air temperature inside the tyres, in degrees Celsius, reported by the tyre-pressure sensors. Tyres warm up while driving, which raises their pressure.
docs.adas_state: Whether the driver-assistance system (for example lane keeping) is switched on and active.
docs.lane_confidence: How sure the camera is that it sees the lane markings, from 0 to 1. Low values come from worn paint, glare or a dirty windscreen.
docs.camera_blockage: How much of the forward camera's view is obstructed, from 0 (clear) to 1 (blocked), for example by dirt or snow.
docs.camera_sharpness: A measure of how sharp the forward camera image is. It falls when the lens is dirty or out of focus.
docs.camera_brightness: The average brightness of the forward camera image. Very low or very high values make lane detection unreliable.
docs.ambient_temperature: The air temperature outside the car, in degrees Celsius.
docs.rain: Whether the rain sensor detects rain on the windscreen.
docs.light: How bright the light outside is, in lux.
docs.heading: The compass direction the car is travelling, in degrees from north.
docs.odometer: The total distance the car has driven in its life, in kilometres.
docs.brake_pad_life: How much of the brake pads' friction material is left, as a percentage. It wears down with use, and the pads need replacing near zero.
docs.brake_temperature: The temperature of the brake discs and pads, in degrees Celsius. It rises sharply under hard or repeated braking and can cause brake fade when too high.
docs.engine_rpm: How fast the combustion engine spins, in revolutions per minute.
docs.engine_torque: The turning force of the combustion engine, in newton-metres.
docs.engine_load: How hard the combustion engine is working, as a percentage of its maximum output.
docs.fuel_rate: How quickly fuel is being burned, in litres per hour.
docs.transmission_temperature: The temperature of the transmission oil, in degrees Celsius.
docs.charging_state: Whether the car is plugged in and charging, and whether it is AC or fast DC charging.
docs.steering_torque: How much force the driver is applying to the steering wheel, in newton-metres. It shows whether hands are on the wheel.
docs.lane_departure: Whether the car is drifting out of its lane without the indicator on.
docs.lead_vehicle_distance: The distance to the vehicle ahead as measured by the radar or camera, in metres.
docs.aeb_state: The state of the automatic emergency braking system: ready, warning or braking.
docs.acc_state: The state of adaptive cruise control: off, standby or controlling the speed.
docs.blindspot_state: Whether the blind-spot monitor currently sees a vehicle beside the car.
docs.humidity: The relative humidity of the outside air, as a percentage.
docs.wind_speed: The speed of the wind, in kilometres per hour.
docs.wind_direction: The direction the wind is coming from, in degrees from north.
docs.brake_fluid_condition: The condition of the brake fluid. Old fluid absorbs water, which lowers its boiling point and weakens braking.
docs.tyre_tread_depth: How deep the grooves in the tyre tread are, in millimetres. Below about 1.6 mm the tyre is unsafe and illegal in many places.
docs.cabin_temperature: The air temperature inside the cabin, in degrees Celsius.
docs.fuel_level: How much fuel is in the tank, as a percentage.
docs.acceleration: How quickly the speed changes, in metres per second squared: positive when speeding up, negative when slowing down. It is derived from the speed trace.
docs.acceleration_magnitude: The size of the acceleration regardless of direction, in metres per second squared, derived from the speed trace.
docs.braking_intensity: How hard the car is slowing down, in units of g (1 g is 9.8 m/s2). Above about 0.3 g counts as hard braking.
docs.horsepower: The motor power expressed in horsepower, derived from torque and speed or from the power signal.
docs.turn_radius: The radius of the circle the car follows in a turn, in metres. Small values mean a sharp turn.
docs.energy_used: The electrical energy taken from the battery, in kilowatt-hours (kWh), added up over the period you ask about.
docs.distance_driven: How far the car travelled, in kilometres, added up from the speed over the period you ask about.
docs.wh_per_km: Energy consumption: how many watt-hours the car uses per kilometre. Lower is more efficient. It rises with speed, cold weather, heating and heavy loads.
docs.regen_energy: The energy given back to the battery by regenerative braking, in kilowatt-hours.
docs.wheel_slip: How much a wheel spins faster or slower than the car is moving, as a ratio. It rises on wet or loose surfaces.
docs.thermal_rise_rate: How fast the battery pack is heating up or cooling down, in degrees Celsius per minute.
docs.range_estimate: How far the car can still go on the charge it has, estimated from the charge left and your recent energy use. It is an estimate, not a measurement.
docs.battery_efficiency: How much of the battery's energy reaches the wheels, as a ratio of motor power to battery power.
docs.adas_disengagement: A moment when the driver-assistance function switched itself off or the driver took over, with the recorded reason.
docs.battery_overheat_warning: A warning raised when the battery pack temperature went above its limit.
docs.diagnostic_code: A diagnostic trouble code (DTC): a coded fault stored by a control unit when it detects a problem, such as low coolant flow.
docs.hard_braking: A braking event stronger than about 0.3 g, recorded with its strength and the speed at which it happened.
docs.hard_acceleration: A burst of acceleration stronger than normal driving, recorded with its strength.
docs.hard_cornering: A turn taken with unusually high sideways acceleration.
docs.tyre_pressure_warning: A warning raised when a tyre's pressure fell below its specification.
docs.tyre_inflation: A record that a tyre was inflated, seen as a sudden rise in its pressure.
docs.low_12v_warning: A warning that the 12 V auxiliary battery voltage fell too low.
docs.service_reminder: A reminder that a scheduled service is due.
docs.camera_blocked: An event raised when the forward camera view was obstructed.
docs.camera_degraded: An event raised when the camera image quality dropped below the level needed for driver assistance.
docs.charging_session: One continuous period of charging, with its start, end, power type and energy delivered.
docs.can_anomaly: An unexpected message pattern on the vehicle's CAN network, such as a missing, duplicated or malformed frame.
docs.any_warning: Any recorded warning or fault: battery, tyre, 12 V, camera, network or diagnostic code.
docs.coolant_flow_drop: A period in which the battery coolant flow fell well below its normal level.
docs.ecu_reset: An event recorded when one of the vehicle's electronic control units restarted, with the unit and the cause (power-on, watchdog timeout, software request or brown-out).
docs.unexpected_shutdown: An event recorded when the vehicle or one of its computers switched off without being asked to, with the likely cause (12 V supply loss, watchdog, high-voltage interlock).
docs.voltage_dip: A short drop of the 12 V supply voltage, recorded with how low it went and for how long. Dips can reset electronics.
docs.sensor_conflict: An event recorded when two sources that report the same quantity (for example the CAN bus and the Android vehicle layer) disagreed by more than their tolerance for several seconds.
docs.aeb_activation: An event recorded when the automatic emergency braking system braked the car by itself, with the speed and the braking strength.
docs.can_error: An event recorded when the CAN network reported error frames, which means messages were corrupted or lost on the wire.
docs.sensor_invalid_reading: An event recorded when a sensor reported a value outside its physically possible range; the value was discarded.
docs.adas_state_change: An event recorded each time the driver-assistance system switched on or off.
docs.overtemp_warning: A warning raised when the engine or coolant temperature went above its limit.
docs.power_derate: An event recorded when the powertrain limited its own power to protect itself (for example a hot motor), which the driver feels as reduced acceleration.
docs.diagnostic_code_cleared: An event recorded when a stored diagnostic trouble code was cleared (by a service tool or because the fault stayed away for enough ignition cycles), with the code. A cleared code is not proof that the fault is gone.
docs.software_update: An event recorded when new software was installed on the vehicle, with the versions before and after.
docs.source_dropout: An event recorded when a data source - a bus or an electronic control unit - stopped sending frames for longer than its usual period while the vehicle was awake. The assistant's own decoder notices it, so it is a recorded fact about the data, not a diagnosis of the cause.
docs.service_log: The text lines written by the vehicle's services (warnings and errors of the QNX services, the Android layer and the controllers). They are stored as data and searched by words; they are never treated as instructions.
docs.diagnostic_status: The state of the vehicle's diagnostic trouble codes as the record shows it: a code is active when its latest event is 'set', cleared when its latest event is 'cleared', and recurring when it was set again after being cleared. A cleared code is not proof that the fault is gone.
docs.engine_oil_temperature: The temperature of the engine oil, in degrees Celsius. It follows the coolant but lags behind it; a warm engine is around 90 to 110 degrees.
docs.fuel_temperature: The temperature of the fuel in the tank or lines, in degrees Celsius.
docs.barometric_pressure: The outside air pressure measured by the engine, in kilopascals. It falls with altitude and in bad weather.
docs.boost_pressure: How much the turbocharger pushes the intake air above the outside pressure, in kilopascals. It is near zero at idle and rises when the engine works hard.
docs.exhaust_gas_temperature: The temperature of the exhaust gas, in degrees Celsius. It rises with engine load and goes very high while the particulate filter burns off its soot.
docs.def_level: How much AdBlue (diesel exhaust fluid, urea) is left in its tank, in percent. The engine uses it to clean nitrogen oxides from the exhaust and will limit power when it runs out.
docs.dpf_soot_load: How full the diesel particulate filter is with soot, in percent. At about 80 percent the engine starts a regeneration, burning the soot off at high exhaust temperature, usually on a long drive.
docs.dpf_regeneration: Whether the engine is burning the soot out of the particulate filter right now: 0 is not active, 1 is active, 2 means a regeneration is needed.
docs.fuel_rail_pressure: The pressure of the fuel in the common rail that feeds the diesel injectors, in kilopascals. It is low at idle and very high under load.
docs.intake_manifold_pressure: The air pressure inside the intake manifold, in kilopascals. It is low at idle and rises towards the outside pressure as the throttle opens.
docs.intake_air_temperature: The temperature of the air entering the engine, in degrees Celsius.
docs.mass_air_flow: How much air the engine is drawing in, in grams per second. The engine computer uses it to decide how much fuel to inject.
docs.lambda: The air-fuel ratio of the exhaust relative to the ideal mixture: 1.0 is ideal, below 1 is rich (too much fuel), above 1 is lean (too little). A petrol engine holds it near 1.0.
docs.short_term_fuel_trim: The quick correction, in percent, that the engine computer adds to or removes from the fuel to keep the mixture ideal. Small swings around zero are normal.
docs.long_term_fuel_trim: The slow, learned correction, in percent, that the engine computer applies to the fuel. A value that stays far from zero (beyond about 10 to 15 percent) points to an air leak, a weak fuel pump or a dirty sensor.
docs.catalyst_temperature: The temperature of the catalytic converter, in degrees Celsius. It must be hot (above about 300 degrees) to clean the exhaust.
docs.ignition_timing: How many degrees before the piston reaches the top the spark fires. The engine computer advances it at light load and retards it when the engine would knock.
